source: Five further user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary, main pages 133, 135, 137, 139 and 141 plus readable preceding-page fragments
normalization_notes: Transcribe all readable Portuguese glossary entries, including preceding-page fragments at the top of each photo. Do not infer entries from missing pages.
Keep printed references and page/source information in JSON only; do not create source categories or treat reference numbers as CEFR levels.
Import lowercase NFC-normalized individual words. Remove punctuation and trailing gender articles; retain actual articles and prepositions within expressions.
Expand ele/ela, esse/essa, este/esta, Está?/Estou? and estar/fazer frio. The o/a annotations on estudante, guia, hóspede and jornalista do not change the spelling.
Separate reflexive se from divertir-se, divorciar-se, esquecer-se, lembrar-se and levantar-se. Separate te from fica-te and preserve the conjugated verb fica.
Retain inflected and conjugated forms: boas, doces, comboios, estatísticas, hábitos, fresca, juntos, diz, diga and estou. Do not invent additional lemmas or word forms.
Keep concrete contextual words such as casa, laranja, triste and pão; ellipses and non-Portuguese explanatory placeholders are not words.
Repeated entries with different senses/references (elevador, estrangeiro, guia, jantar, letra and ficar) retain all source contexts while sharing one normalized word record.
German glosses are source data. Translate the individual Portuguese words independently, with complete expressions retained for context.
